blocks.content: If any question arises whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion or not, the decision of the Governor shall be final.

rows: Explicitly mentioned in the text of the Constitution
Derived from prevailing political situations and exigencies
Reserving a bill for the consideration of the President (Art. 200)
Appointment of Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority
Recommending the imposition of President's Rule (Art. 356)
Dismissal of the council of ministers when it fails to prove confidence in the Legislative Assembly
Determining the royalty amount payable to an autonomous Tribal District Council
Dissolution of the Legislative Assembly if the Council of Ministers loses its majority

items: Unlike the President of India, who has only situational discretion, the Governor possesses both constitutional and situational discretion.
The validity of anything done by the Governor shall not be called into question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion.
Recommending the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356 is a key constitutional discretion frequently tested in civil services exams.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 163 explicitly grants the Governor constitutional discretion, making the Governor's discretionary scope wider than that of the President.
If any question arises whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion, the decision of the Governor is final and cannot be challenged.
Situational discretion arises during political exigencies, such as appointing a Chief Minister when no single party enjoys a clear majority.
The Governor can reserve certain state bills for the consideration of the President under Article 200 as part of discretionary duties.
The Governor acts as a crucial link between the Centre and the State, particularly when recommending President's Rule under Article 356.
